messages:
Carmen: Quick thread 11: propose a tiny 'runbook snippet' in the Dedicated provisioning docs that explains the order of operations when fallback triggers (what gets checked first: reserved capacity, per-variant quota, regional failover). We keep getting support tickets where customers assume fallback steals reserved capacity. cc @kevin @sre-jen

Kevin: Strong +1. We should add a short ordered list (2-3 steps) and a compact CLI snippet to inspect which condition fired. Keep it super short and copy-pasteable.

SRE-Jen: Ops notes to include: (1) check ReservedCapacityUtilization metric first; (2) check per-variant quota/429s on fallback variant; (3) verify tenant_labels.isolation and any preemption events. Also mention that fallback is best-effort and does not lower the contractual reserved throughput.

Docs-bot: Draft PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/7007 (runbook micro-section)

Carmen: Proposed micro runbook text (concise):
- Step 1: Verify reserved capacity usage in Console (ReservedCapacityUtilization). If <100%, proceed to step 2.
- Step 2: Check fallback quota and recent 429s for the fallback variant.
- Step 3: Confirm no preemption events affected routing (tenant_labels and recent evictions).
- Quick note: Fallback = overflow path; reserved contract remains intact.

Kevin: CLI/Logs snippet (copyable):
```bash
# recent fallback requests and throttle events for tenant
redwoodctl logs query --tenant your-tenant --filter 'routing.variant=fallback OR routing.event=fallback_throttle' --last 15m

# reserved capacity util
redwoodctl metrics query --metric ReservedCapacityUtilization --tenant your-tenant --last 15m
```

Ops-Lee: Small ops caveat: in cross-region failover cases the UI may show fallback=true when the active region uses a different model variant; clarify that in the runbook. Add a one-line: "Cross-region variant mismatch may look like fallback in some Console views."

Billing-Alfie: Billing note: all routed requests (including fallback) count toward tenant billing and may be billed at the fallback variant rate. Add a one-liner so customers know why invoice line-items change.

Carmen: I'll add a tiny FAQ entry too: "Why did 30% of my requests route to fallback?" -> "Check fallback_policy.max_fallback_pct, reserved utilization, and per-request routing_preferences (SDK can opt out of fallback)."

Kevin: Suggest also a tiny YAML snippet showing a diagnostic-friendly fallback config (explicit max_fallback_pct, throttle action = delay) and a recommended cooldown: 75-120s for most dedicated fleets.

Carmen: YAML snippet (diagnostic-friendly):
```yaml
scalePolicy:
  target_qps: 120
  cooldown_s: 90  # recommended: 75-120s depending on fleet size
  fallbackModel: rdl-medium-q1
  fallback_policy:
    max_fallback_pct: 25
    fallback_throttle_action: delay
```

SRE-Jen: LG. Add ops troubleshooting bullets under the runbook: how to temporarily disable fallback (CLI), how to bump fallback quota, and how to enable full-trace for 10-30m for a tenant. Keep each bullet one line.

Carmen: Will include CLI to toggle fallback off for a tenant and a link to internal quota increase flow. Draft PR text will be micro (6-8 lines).

Docs-bot: PR updated with runbook micro-section, CLI/YAML snippets, FAQ, and ops bullets. Reviewers requested: @kevin @sre-jen @billing-alfie

Kevin: I'll give it a quick pass and merge if wording is tight. Thanks all! :shipit:
